correctness.rationale: For the strict chamber \(H/r^2<s<1+H/r^3\), the outer-state magnitude recurrence \(g(z)=r(z-1)\) satisfies \(g^3(s)=sr^3-(r+r^2+r^3)<1\), excluding four consecutive outer states. Every length \(n=4q+j\) prefix therefore has at least \(q\) inner derivatives, giving \(|(T^n)'|\ge s^q r^{3q+j}\). The strict eight-cycle witness \(u=(sr^3-r-r^2-r^3)/(1+sr^3)\) stays on the inner–outer–outer–outer repeated itinerary because \(sr^2>H\), and its return multiplier is \((sr^3)^2\), attaining the lower exponent bound. With \(\rho=(sr^3)^{1/4}>1\), the finite-time estimate gives uniform exponential expansion; for \(sr^3\le1\) this cycle refutes it. The exact rational checker passed six parameter instances, the canonical published orbit, and 150 neutral samples; finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: A fixed-point-free map used to generate chaotic signals has published numerical estimates of positive Lyapunov exponents. Positivity of an observed exponent does not imply a positive worst-case exponent over all starting states. The exact infimum over every branch-regular initial state in a maximal-three-outer-step chamber, plus the necessary-and-sufficient sharp boundary \(sr^3=1\) for uniform derivative expansion, determines a substantive global dynamical invariant. The known period-eight witness is used solely to establish optimality; the novel mathematical content is the uniform all-itinerary bound.
